long_biography.plain_text:
Raised at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, Raymond Floyd learned golf from his father and turned professional in 1961. He won on the PGA Tour at 20 and developed into one of his era's most formidable competitors. His 22 tour titles included the Masters, two PGA Championships and the U.S. Open, giving him major victories across three decades.

Floyd remained successful after moving to the senior circuit, where he added 14 PGA Tour Champions titles and four senior majors. He also captained the United States Ryder Cup team and built a selective course-design practice. That second career translated his experience of championship layouts and strategic shot-making into courses intended to challenge skilled players while remaining enjoyable for a broader field.
